budget.estimate_verdict: NO. The 480 core-minute estimate covers the WHOLE proposal (225x65 and 449x129 at alpha 10, then full ladders at alpha 0 and 15). Measured this session and cross-checked against two prior-session attempts, a single (grid, alpha) pair on the medium rung alone needs an estimated 11,700-30,300 core-minutes just to reach a 30-convective-unit window -- a window ALREADY SHOWN insufficient for stationarity on the coarse rung -- and roughly 117,000-303,000 core-minutes for the 'hundreds of convective units' the proposal's own rationale says is required. That is 24x to 630x the entire 480-minute budget for one rung, before the stationarity gate can even be evaluated. The estimate undercounts the time-accurate approach's true cost by 1-3 orders of magnitude.

stationarity_gate.verdict: NOT REACHED, not a pass and not a drift-fail. The run never approaches the averaging window start (0.4 x end_time in run_naca_transient's convention); halves_drift() has nothing to evaluate. This is a distinct, upstream failure mode from a drifting mean -- it is reported as such, not forced through the gate.

rungs.comparison_vs_cfl3d: None computed. No coefficient may be quoted from 0.005 convective units of march; doing so would violate the no-fabrication rule.
cause: Adaptive Courant-limited timestep (maxCo 1.5) plateaus at deltaT ~3.7e-5 on the medium grid, versus an effective ~0.041 units/step measured on the coarse grid's own transient run (30 units / 735 steps) -- about a 1,100x smaller step. Combined with 4x the cell count per step, this yields the measured ~9,700x slower wall-clock rate per convective unit than the coarse rung's transient march.

Independent, measured contributing cause: the converted TMR medium mesh has severe cell-quality defects. checkMesh on the same mesh (demo-output/website/tmr/runs/naca-a10-medium/log.checkMesh) reports max aspect ratio 26446226.94 on 1822 cells, 170 severely non-orthogonal faces (>70 degrees), and 'Failed 1 mesh checks'. Consistent with that, the confirmatory log shows the pressure PCG solve repeatedly hitting its 1000-iteration cap without full convergence ('No Iterations 1000' on both p and pFinal blocks) -- each of the already-too-few affordable timesteps is itself expensive.

Seeding from the developed steady field (tried 2026-07-26) does not rescue this: it crawls even slower (5.0e-6 units/s) than the cold start, working through an impulsive adjustment shock, the same failure mode already documented for the coarse/alpha0 rung in naca0012_status.json.
rungs.lesson: Time-accurate averaging on this grid is not a budget problem that more core-minutes inside the 480 estimate can fix; it is a 1-3 order of magnitude gap. MPI parallelism would not close it either: the bottleneck is timestep COUNT under a Courant limit set by cell geometry, not per-step throughput, so adding ranks raises core-minute cost without proportionally cutting wall-clock steps needed.

rungs.reason: Fine is the next TMR family doubling (4x medium's cell count) with correspondingly finer near-wall and leading-edge spacing. Extrapolating the coarse-to-medium collapse already measured (~9700x slowdown per convective unit for one grid doubling) makes a fine-rung transient attempt certain to be far less affordable than medium's already-measured 24x-630x-over-budget result. Spending foreground core-minutes to confirm a near-certain outcome was judged not worthwhile; this is a documented, reasoned stop, not an oversight.

overall_lesson: The coarse rung remains the only trustworthy NACA 0012 lift/drag number this project has. The medium and fine rungs' blocker (a wake-driven oscillation that never decays under the steady solver) cannot be resolved by throwing the proposal's 480-core-minute time-accurate budget at it: the honest, now twice-measured (2026-07-26 and 2026-07-28) rate shows that budget is 1-3 orders of magnitude short for even ONE (grid, alpha) pair. Closing the medium/fine rungs needs either a fundamentally cheaper approach (fixed larger implicit step with a stability study rather than a Courant-limited adaptive one, a compressible/preconditioned solver matching CFL3D's own numerics, or a coarser but valid stationarity target) or a budget reset that is explicit about needing tens of thousands of core-minutes per rung, not hundreds.
